message:
test(evidence-audit): execute the streamKey guarantee of the envelope facts

The seven envelope-native facts were certified to stream under their
envelope only by reading their bodies. Two assertions per fact now run
it: the stream key is the envelope and equals subject(). The test is
tagged eIDAS-event-integrity. Also records the monolog-bundle recipe in
symfony.lock and patches six Symfony components with security
advisories.

build(deps): update 51 packages and bound the open constraints

Each package moves to its latest release inside the pinned minor, and
the open version constraints are bounded so the next update cannot
arrive by accident. Also drops 18 redundant case-variant entries from
the cspell word list.

docs: reconcile the docs with the code and keep the design trail in the repo

One pass with two jobs: make the documentation say what the code does
today, and move design knowledge that lived in untracked notes into
tracked docs.

feat(envelope): declare per-recipient document access in the domain and application

Any recipient could list and download every document of an envelope.
Access is now declared per recipient and per document, and the read
paths refuse when nothing is declared.
feat(envelope): enforce document access in the read and download adapters

test(envelope): cover per-recipient document access

Covers the declaration, the fail-closed refusals and the list and
download paths for a recipient who may not see a document.

fix(envelope): hold signing and sight as independent grants, not one level

Signing does not imply sight. On a multi-drop waybill each destination
signs the joint document while reading only their own leg, so the two
are now declared separately.

fix(envelope): refuse to send when a signer is shown no document at all

Signing without sight is fine per document, but a signer who can see
none of the documents has nothing to sign, so the send is refused.
Merge develop into feat/per-recipient-document-access: resolve the LIVE_SCHEMA conflict

feat(notification): render the designed HTML email beside the text part

EMAIL deliveries went out as plain text while the design existed only as
a wireframe. Each purpose and locale now carries an HTML part rendered
next to the text one.

fix(envelope): apply two pre-merge reviews of per-recipient document access

Two full review passes were applied on top of the branch; the full suite
passes with the fixes.
Merge feat/per-recipient-document-access: documents are visible per recipient, fail-closed

feat(envelope): add the Field entity, every placed rectangle is one thing

A field is a placed rectangle on a document, discriminated by type;
signature marks are fields of type SIGNATURE instead of a separate
model.

feat(fields): back the options columns with value objects and let the signer see fields

Two passes of ADR-0040 committed together: options land in the domain as
value objects, then the second pass publishes them to the signer through
the same files.

feat(fields): one field, many rectangles, one value

A field is one thing a participant is asked for; where it appears is a
bounded list of occurrences in envelope.field_occurrence, each with its
own page and geometry (ADR-0041).

docs(fields): record the definition/occurrence split in ADR-0041

The ADR states the decision and the rejected alternative, correlating
sibling fields through a source_field_id self-reference.

fix(envelope): the field id is minted by the server, not chosen by the caller

POST /envelopes/{id}/fields no longer accepts field_id. It was the only
one of eight authoring endpoints that took an id from the caller.

feat(fields): navigation order is read off the geometry, not stored beside it

envelope.field.ordinal is dropped. Where a participant meets a field
follows from where its rectangles are: document position, page, then
vertical origin.

fix(envelope,session): apply the field review: 5 blockers, 12 corrections, 4 backlog rows

The review verdict was to merge after fixes. Everything it raised was
re-verified against the tree before the fixes were applied.
Merge feat/envelope-field-entity: fields with definitions, occurrences and derived order

docs: add authoring rules written from past defects and fix four false claims

Adds a section of seven rules to the contributor guide, each tied to a
failure that shipped with a green build, and corrects the repo rule on
migrations and three statements that were false.

docs(auth): decide two-gate signer authentication (ADR-0044) and plan it

Signer authentication is modelled as two independently declared gates on
one session timeline: access (get in, read, fill) and signing (commit
the act). The envelope and notification domain models are reconciled
with the decision.

docs(identity-access): document authenticated requests and the credential model

Before this change every write path trusted its caller: tenant scope
came from an unverified X-Tenant-Id header and the acting user from an
unverified header too. Requests are now authenticated from a verified
credential.
feat(identity-access)!: add credential routes, settings and architecture rules
feat(identity-access)!: carry the verified actor through the envelope use cases
feat(identity-access)!: read tenant and actor from the credential at the request edge
feat(identity-access)!: add the credential, crypto and request-edge adapters
feat(identity-access)!: expose the identity routes and move envelope tests to credentials
test(foundation): cover the credential, crypto and http units
test(identity-access): cover the application, persistence and unit layers

test(identity-access): cover authenticated requests in notification, session, signing

With the change complete the full suite passes; every request in the
acceptance tests now carries a real credential.

docs(backlog): re-anchor the rows the identity-access merge orphaned

Merging a branch falsifies every note that points at it, and the grep
for the branch name was not run at the merge.

docs: name the consolidation beside every migration that no longer exists

Dangling migration references now say which migration replaced them.
Also adds the two ways to get an untrustworthy test run to the tests
README, such as a worker competing for broker messages.
Merge develop into feat/notification-email-html: take develop's channel prose

docs: fix the id sweeps that return nothing and give the frontend handoff a home

Both uniqueness sweeps in the task and ADR guides returned nothing when
run from inside their own directory. Cross-repo work is two coordinated
PRs, so a contract change here needs a stated place and convention for
the handoff.
Merge develop into docs/two-gate-signer-auth: keep both sides of the ADR index

docs(auth): renumber the two-gate ADR to 0049 and close its open questions

The identity-access work reached develop first and took 0044 to 0048, so
the ADR is renumbered. Closing its five open questions showed a minted
credential must sit behind the gate. Also extracts the delivery-failure
repair into its own task and re-reconciles the envelope model.

fix(event-log): a broker outage no longer burns the poison counter; show quarantine

The relay could quarantine healthy facts when the broker was down
(BL-16), and nothing told anyone it had. The counted try now wraps only
the failure that proves a fact is poison, and quarantined facts can be
read.
Merge develop into feat/event-relay-dead-letter-visibility
docs(adr-0031): record the poison-counter correction and the quarantine read side
Merge docs/task-conventions: task record convention, TASK-024, handoff home
Merge develop into feat/notification-email-html
Merge feat/notification-email-html: the designed HTML email is sent beside the text part

docs(event-path): plan the three silent drops and correct the ADR on them

TASK-026 records three independent ways a fact in platform.event_log
never reaches a recipient with nothing raised anywhere a human looks.
Merge docs/event-path-silent-drops: TASK-026 and the ADR-0031 correction

docs(auth): give the session credential a material and make the signing token opaque

ADR-0049 decided that passing the access gate mints a credential, not a
flag; this says what it is made of. Also admits one inbound command
surface in Notification, retracts a queue that never existed, and
corrects what the two-gate ADR got wrong.

docs(notification): plan Spanish email without the ICU chain (TASK-027)

Ships Spanish by the short route: an es key plus the locale resolution
chain two comments already describe. Corrects the reasoning that made
the ICU chain look cheap.
Merge docs/spanish-email-and-locale: plan for Spanish email

feat(notification): Spanish email copy, written around two genders nobody knows

First step of TASK-027: the es catalog for both purposes plus the guards
that keep it honest. No schema, wire contract or locale resolution yet.
Merge feat/spanish-email-locale: Spanish email catalog

Merge develop: renumber two tasks and seven backlog rows that collided

Two branches numbered against the same snapshot of develop at the same
time, and develop moved first. Both id sweeps were clean when they were
run, so the collision came from the stale snapshot.

docs(auth): stop citing a policy-override chain that has no level behind it

ADR-0049 section 2.8 described a tenant to platform precedence that does
not exist. Also records that the limiter store is shared and fails open,
and adds the crosswalk rows three ADRs were missing.

docs(adr): land ADR-0052 and declare twig as a runtime dependency

TASK-024 was blocked on an ADR it owed: ADR-0038 had rejected Twig.
ADR-0052 allows it to compose the email layout at authoring time and
never to interpolate a value. Only the dependency is added, with no
bundle or template yet.
Merge feat/twig-scoped-to-email: ADR-0052 and the twig dependency

feat(envelope): a recipient may state the language to be written to in

TASK-027, second step: a nullable locale on envelope.recipient, exposed
on RecipientView and the envelope query, and accepted by AddRecipient.

feat(notification): resolve the locale recipient, tenant, system, defaulting to Spanish

This makes the Spanish copy reachable; until now nothing passed a
non-default locale. Also hands the contract change to the front ends and
hardens the field: a blank locale is refused at both ends, bounded at
the wire and escaped at the sink.

feat(event-log): add a replay command for one quarantined fact

TASK-026, first step. The command was complete but needed one PHPStan
exemption for a hard delete, which landed separately. Also corrects the
second half of the BL-113 pair in the task.

docs(task-027,backlog): close the record and home five deferrals

The status clauses saying later steps were not started were false, and
the deferrals now have backlog rows instead of loose notes.
Merge develop into feat/recipient-locale-chain: resolve BACKLOG and TASK-024 conflicts

build(phpstan): sanction the one hard delete the replay needs and realize ADR-0031

Unblocks the replay command of TASK-026. The reasoning was already
written in the task and is restated next to the exemption.
Merge develop into feat/event-log-replay-command
Merge develop into feat/event-log-golden-payload-bytes

test(event-log): freeze the payloads already in the log and census what must be frozen

ADR-0031 names the gap the round-trip tests cannot see: they serialize
and deserialize with the same code. Also pins the replay command's exit
codes.

feat(envelope,notification): a recipient we could not reach, and the way back

Implements TASK-025: a delivery failure is recorded as a fact on the
recipient, and the sender can correct the address and re-invite.
Merge develop into feat/recipient-delivery-failure-2

test(event-log): freeze the bytes of the two events TASK-025 adds

GoldenPayloadBytesTest failed naming RECIPIENT_CORRECTED and
RECIPIENT_DELIVERY_FAILED, which is the census working. Also records
what TASK-025 realized in the models and ADRs.

feat(notification): compose the email layout in Twig and keep the email identical

The HTML part of the EMAIL channel moves out of about 400 lines of PHP
heredocs into templates/notification/. A follow-up audit corrected prose
that claimed more than the wiring does.
Merge develop into feat/recipient-delivery-failure-2: resolve the BACKLOG conflict

fix(envelope,notification): prove the return path, stop mailing links early

Applies the eleven findings of the three validations of TASK-025.

build: install the rate limiter and declare the Redis extension already in use

Only the dependencies, to unblock TASK-022. Also confirms the direction
of ADR-0051 and corrects a prerequisite that was half false.

fix(event-log): reject an undecodable message instead of dying on it

TASK-026. A message the codec cannot decode used to take the worker down
with it; it is now rejected and sent to the dead letter queue.
Merge origin/develop into feat/event-decoding-failure-dead-letter

chore(config): regenerate reference.php after symfony/rate-limiter landed

rate_limiter.enabled defaults to true now that the component is
installed.

feat(session-credential): add the credential material and its refresh store

TASK-029, first step: the two Authn cases, the JWT codec with a closed
claim set, and the renewal credential's rotation state, registered as
kind sr in ADR-0045.

feat(session-credential): add the two listeners, the partition and the renewal route

Intermediate commit on the branch: eleven acceptance tests still fail
until opening a session mints the credential, which the next commit
does.

feat(session-credential): opening a session issues the credential pair

Closes what the previous commit left open: the open route now mints the
session and renewal credentials, and the spec stops abstaining.

test(session-credential): add the twelve acceptance bars and the idle clock

Lands the tests for TASK-029 section 5 and fixes a defect they did not
find, a clock that nobody had built.

docs(task-029): realize the records, and promote ADR-0050 to Accepted

The exercise is green and every bar names its artifact. Also sweeps
prose the partition made false, kills four escaped mutants, and explains
why the GRANT CONNECT is redundant today and load-bearing later.

feat(auth): mint the three refusal kinds and the two-gate declaration vocabulary

ADR-0029 left the auth-refusal kinds unminted for want of an aggregate
guard that used them; TASK-021 is that exercise.

feat(envelope): the recipient carries its two gates, its verifier and its auth generation

The declaration reaches storage as five new columns on
envelope.recipient.

feat(signing-token): reserve the credential segment and add the lookup store

TASK-028. Reserves the signing token's segment in the published grammar,
locks the disclosure bar against the token that still fails it, and adds
the digest-keyed lookup store. The migration needs a database role that
does not exist yet.

feat(signing-token): add the resolver and the write path for the lookup store

TASK-028 read and issuance. SigningTokenDirectory is declared in
Foundation because the request edge lives there, and issuance goes
through a security definer function. The new table is classified in the
schema conformance test.

feat(signing-token): the credential a recipient receives is now opaque

The cutover: both minting sites issue an ADR-0045 st credential through
Session. Adds the purge of expired tokens and closes TASK-028 in the
records.

feat(signing-token): close the cutover window and retire the codec

BL-148 and BL-151. The edge accepts one encoding and the old codec
classes are removed, which also fixes a third minting path nobody had
listed. A settled notification occasion stops holding the recipient's
credential (BL-113).

feat(session): two gates, a budget and a lockout a sender can lift

The Session half of the two-gate model, whose last piece is the lockout
that a sender can lift.

feat(session): the act consumes its challenge and a dead envelope refuses both gates

Three gaps the documentation pass found in the code just written.

feat(auth): add routes 3 and 5, the child tables and the published contract

Committed with eleven tests failing from one root cause, fixed in the
next commit.

test(session): the ceremony fixtures author the envelope they name

Ten of the eleven failing tests shared one cause, fixtures naming an
envelope they never created. Also makes the availability port
Envelope's, as ADR-0013 describes.

Merge origin/develop into feat/two-gate-signer-auth: take the opaque signing token

TASK-028 retired SigningTokenCodec in favour of a store-backed token.

fix(session): the open gate is a fact about the passage, not about the declaration

A recipient with both gates declared could never sign. Also fixes the
32-byte floor comment that lost its example in the merge and updates the
TASK-021 records.

feat(auth): the lockout crosses back and an idle grant can be withdrawn

Two surfaces had no caller anywhere in src/, which mutation testing
cannot see.

feat(auth): add the four milestone facts the design promised

The design lists five milestones that reach the event log; only one
existed.

test(session): drive routes 3 and 5 over HTTP

No test requested session/auth, so the descriptor and submit routes were
never exercised end to end.

test(session): the two hard bars and the child tables nothing round-tripped

Two overlapping wrong codes must spend two attempts, not one, and the
new tables are now read back after writing.

fix(contract): declare a missing 404 and two refusals, and read the whole enum census

Also adds tests for four surfaces the validation passes found untested,
an index on session.auth_challenge(session_id), and closes the TASK-021
record with its deviations and handoff.

docs(ddd): reconcile the domain model and fix the lockout reset that evicted no one

The model still described the work as designed but not built. The
security audit found the reset never evicted anyone while the contract
said it did. ADR-0029 now records the kinds as minted and ADR-0049 is
accepted.

Merge TASK-021: two-gate signer authentication

The signer can be asked to prove something per recipient at two
independently declared gates.

feat(auth): deliver one-time codes over email, domain and application

TASK-022, step 2 of 3. Swaps a delivered verifier into the gates
TASK-021 built, and splits ensuring a challenge from re-sending it.
feat(auth): deliver one-time codes over email, adapters

test(auth): cover one-time code delivery over email

Covers delivery, the ensure versus re-send split and the rate limits.
